parole.significato: A longfin tuna, a large marine fish (Thunnus alalunga) of warm seas, having edible flesh.
parole.testo: From Portuguese albacor, from Arabic اَلْبَكُورَة (al-bakūra, “the young camels”).

parole.significato: A traditional Portuguese unit of dry measure, equal to 13.1–19.3 liters in different 19th-century contexts.
parole.testo: From Portuguese alqueire, from Arabic الكَيْل (al-kayl, “a measure”), from ك ي ل (k y l).

parole.significato: A tall Afro-Brazilian hand drum, traditionally having its shell made of jacaranda wood.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Portuguese atabaque, from Arabic الطَّبَق (aṭ-ṭabaq, “plate”).

parole.significato: An Indian trader, merchant, cashier, or money changer.
parole.testo: From Portuguese baniano, from Arabic بَنِيَان (baniyān), from Gujarati વાણિયો (vāṇiyo, “merchant”), from Sanskrit वाणिज (vāṇijá), from earlier वणिज् (vaṇíj, “merchant, trader”). Borrowed from Portuguese beringela, from Old Galician-Portuguese berengenha, borrowed from Arabic بَاذِنْجَان (bāḏinjān), borrowed from Classical Persian بَاذِنْگَان (bāzingān), borrowed from Sanskrit वातिङ्गण (vātiṅgaṇa), from Proto-Dravidian *waẓVtV. Doublet of aubergine, malidzano, and melongene.

parole.significato: A squall or violent rainstorm coming from the south.
parole.testo: From Portuguese Sumatra, from Arabic سُومَطْرَة (sūmaṭra), from Malay Sumatera, from Sanskrit समुद्र (samudra, “sea”). Mentioned in the 11th century in Sanskrit as समुद्रभूमि (samudrabhūmi, “land of Sumatra”), gradually replacing the earlier सुवर्णद्वीप (suvarṇadvīpa).

parole.significato: A severe tropical cyclone; an intense, rotating storm.
parole.testo: English texts mention typhon, tiphon as a Greek word for "whirlwind" since at least the 1550s, referring to Ancient Greek τυφῶν (tuphôn), τυφώς (tuphṓs, “whirlwind”) (the latter attested since Aeschylus), Τυφῶν (Tuphôn, “Typhon, father of the winds”). parole.significato: An old monetary unit of Portuguese India from the 16th to 19th centuries, equal to 300 reis.
parole.testo: From Portuguese xarafin, from Arabic اَشْرَاف (ašrāf), plural form of شَرِيف (šarīf, “highborn”).
